utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances for the day, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, Counsel, everyone in the courtroom. Mark Harmon, Lorna Bolton, and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to all the parties in the proceedings. Novak Lukic, Tina Drolec Chad Mair, and Alex Fielding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Good morning, Mr Krayishnik. Just to remind you, sir, that you're still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Bolton, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Krayishnik, how are you?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm all tangled up. One moment. There we are. Mr. Krayishnik, I read over the transcript of the conversation we had yesterday, and I just had a few kind of housekeeping questions I wanted to ask you about before we continue our conversation from yesterday. At page 9.490 of the transcript, I asked you a question about the mechanism you had for proving to people in Canada that you had delivered the aid as promised, and your response was: "Yes. It was video-taped, camera. Mostly Mr. Lesic had." Did Mr. Lesic own a video camera?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. When we ended yesterday's session, you may remember that we were talking about -- I had just shown you some footage from the 17th of July, 1995, that you identified as being in Crna Rijeka, and I asked you the question - and this was at page 9526 of yesterday's transcript - if you recall to arrange the transport for you, and you said that you didn't remember. And I'm just going to try to refresh your memory on that point. We started yesterday's session with a video recording of General Mladic in the hospital boardroom on the 16th of July. Do you recall that footage, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And I've told you I have a transcript from that footage, and I just wish to refer you to part of what he said during that session.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And for the assistance of the court and my friends, this appears at page 2 of that transcript, which is 65 ter 9597.01. And at the bottom of the page, around line 31 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Madam Bolton. You haven't given us 9597.01. You have given us 9597.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I believe, Your Honour, that yesterday we were talking about the fact that there was a transcript that corresponded with the video, and we were using the video. My friend has the transcript and it's available, and I'll be seeking to tender it into evidence. It's 9597.01.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. I remember you referring to 9597.01 yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Oh, you would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I specifically asked you -- and that was after you referred to 9597, and I specifically asked you what are you dealing with now? Are you dealing with 9597, or are you dealing with 9597.1? You said you were dealing with 9597. And 9597 went from 1 minute to 1.1 -- 1.6 minutes, and it went right up to 48.43.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. To make things clearer then, perhaps we could display 9597.01, which is the transcript which is of the video that we watched yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So that everybody can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: .1 is the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: .01 is the transcript that corresponds with the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Which we haven't seen so far.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: No, you haven't seen it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Alright, so looking at the English version you have before you in 9597.01, page 2, and at the bottom of the page you'll see there's some text that starts around line 31. General Mladic was saying: "With all these people who participated in this. You should make a list and then you will come to my place and then I will give you a letter of appreciation, and we will list all the people who took part in this process of requiring this particular spare part; they will have my signature ..." If we could turn the page, please. And if we could scroll up to the top of the next page. It then says: "... which proves that this has been delivered here. It's all on the camera. Do we understand each other?" And then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, the English has --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And then we're on page -- I think we're still on page 3, are we now?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could we scroll down to the bottom of the page, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And now at the bottom of page 3 in the English version we have General Mladic saying: "This spare part will arrive. I'll take care of that. In the morning the car will be waiting for you at the intercontinental. We will solve the problem. I'll be waiting for you there as well." Does that assist you at all in recalling who arranged for the cars to come and pick you up?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who arranged it. As you already said that he said that he's going to arrange. So I wasn't paying attention who would bring the vehicle or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay, so you're not sure then.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I've finished with that document for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: We left off yesterday talking about the location of Crna Rijeka and Han Pijesak, and you had assisted us by drawing those on a map. And today I just want to show you a map to assist you in locating Belgrade relative to Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And so if I could have Exhibit P00187, please. And I'm going to ask the Registrar to zoom in to the area in the upper right-hand corner of the map, if he could, and we still want to be able to see a little bit farther down on the map. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Can you see Belgrade on that map, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And I don't -- I don't know that it's necessary to have you circle it. It's pretty apparent. Can you also see on that map Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. You're having trouble locating it?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. If it would assist you, sir, if you look over where the writing is "Drina S.0. 3."

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Can you see it in that vicinity, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's kind of -- the picture is not very clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Can we zoom in on the area of Drina S.0. 3 for the gentleman. And if not I have a paper -- a blow-up I can show you, sir, if that's too hard to see. Can you see it now, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Han Pijesak, yes, I do. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could then zoom back out to the original image we were looking at there showing Belgrade. Okay. Do you recall, sir, when you were travelling in these cars to -- on the 17th of July, 1995, from Belgrade to Han Pijesak, do you recall what route you took?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I -- I assume that we did a thing like we always did, and I remember we did cross the Vlasenica, and -- and went up to the mountain.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. First of all, where did you -- you said you assumed you took the same route you always took. Do you recall where you always crossed over from the FRY into the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually to Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Usually through?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Can we --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Can I file this map as an exhibit, please, and I'd like to go back to Exhibit P2400.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ma'am, I thought you said this was P187.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: This is P187, and I wish to switch to a map that has greater detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you say can I file this map as an exhibit, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Can -- we've shown the witness this map so he could orientate himself as to where Belgrade was relative to Han Pijesak, and I'd like to -- if we could make a photo of this blow-up, what we're showing him now, what's on the screen right now, that's what I'd like to file. So that the record's clear what he's been shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Except that there are no markings on it, and this is already in evidence. This is the problem. The whole map is -- or do you want just this part?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I just want this screen, just so it's clear what we were showing him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. P187 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that becomes Exhibit P2796. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And if I could have P2400, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, can you locate, or can you see on this map the road that you think you took from Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to need a pen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe we come this way --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... Okay, we're going to -- sorry, Mr. Krayishnik, I don't mean to interrupt. We're just going to get the usher to help you with the pen that actually works on that screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems to me that Ms. Bolton is leading the witness too much, because he said a minute ago that he doesn't know which route they had taken, that he thinks that they had taken the usual route. Now Ms. Bolton is eliciting something from the witness, and the witness replied that he isn't sure whether on that occasion he went by that road. And I think that this map don't show Bijeljina. The -- my learned friend is insisting on this map probably because she wants to corroborate her case, but this witness has nothing to do with that. These red dots, as we know, show the locations of mass executions, but the witness is more familiar and more comfortable with the map that shows Bijeljina and Belgrade. I think that in this way the witness is being led too much to say something about which he is not certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Well, first of all, the wording of my question was, Can you locate or see on this map the road you think that you took. So that was consistent with what the witness says, which is he thinks he took the route they always take. So I was not putting words into his mouth. And secondly, until my friend mentioned it, I don't think that the witness was aware of what the red dots meant. He's now pointed out to him. I'm certainly not relying on the map for that purpose. This happens to be a map that has the greatest detail of this area, and I'm asking the witness to indicate what route he took. I'm a little concerned that some of these objections keep being made in the presence of the witness, so he keeps now being told information that he wasn't privy to previously. And if there's going to be any more objections or discussions of this nature, I'd ask that my friend have the witness step out of the courtroom before he makes that kind of objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The problem, Madam Bolton, with your question is that you say can you locate or can you see on this map the road you think that you took from Bijeljina. There is no Bijeljina on the map. This is the point.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The fact that Bijeljina itself isn't on the map doesn't mean that the road that leads out of Bijeljina isn't on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure, but then --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And the witness was about to show with the electronic pen the road leading out of Bijeljina, at least the part that's visible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And he will show us from where Bijeljina is on the map, because he's got to start from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to ask him where Bijeljina is and then to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That was not the question. You asked -- the question asked was to show the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Well, firstly, I wanted to see if the road was actually on the map. Then I was going to ask him to say where relative in map does show Bijeljina, but where would be Bijeljina be would approximately, and then mark the route.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are standing up, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't want to suggest anything. The map itself has a legend as to what the red dots are, and the OTP are showing this to the witness. I still believe that it is much better for the witness to use the other map that he had seen. He was much more comfortable with it. And the witness said himself yesterday that he was much more comfortable with the map that was shown to him previously than this one. Obviously during the proofing the OTP showed him a different map. It was probably the usual kind of map that we all know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know what map they showed him. Perhaps you know it. I don't. I think, Madam Bolton, you're either going to have to change your question and ask him to first show approximately where he thinks Bijeljina is, or you're going to show him a map with just Bijeljina on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you, Your Honour. Let's start, then, so there's no confusion by going back to the map we were just using that was just entered as Exhibit P2796.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Is that large enough for you to read, sir, or clear enough for you to read?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Barely. I can barely read Zvornik, and I'm not even sure if it says Zvornik or not, which is down here.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes. I see where you're referring to. I'll see if the print copy I have is any better, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I wonder if I could show the print copy, my friend. It's a little bit clearer, I think, than the copy on the screen. That may or may not assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: On that print -- colour print copy, sir, are you able to find Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it's here, but also, and that's what I think, it here.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. You have a regular -- okay. Now having located it on the colour map, can you circle it on -- with the electronic pen on the map that's before us. Oops, they've moved it.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Are you going to put it back? Right here. I believe that's it. No, it's not either. Did I miss it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you want to erase that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may help. Wouldn't it be best given the fact that the witness has a hard copy in front of him on the ELMO, why doesn't he mark on the hard copy, because obviously he's more comfortable with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay, is it something you can find on the hard copy, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me look at it. I'm not very good at it because I'm not that familiar with this geography. I need assistance here. I cannot locate it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, if it will assist you --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know we did come through Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, can --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know we went through Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Can you locate Janja on the map, sir? Can you see that? And I should maybe spell that for you because sometimes my pronunciations aren't great.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you pronounce it good, Janja.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Janja, I'm looking for it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If it assists, it's north of Zvornik, sir.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, you're looking north of Zvornik, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. You see the border?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Drina is the border.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes. You see the Drina? If you follow the Drina north ...

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you see Janja? Next to the word -- basically opposite the word "Semberija."

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zvornik, I don't see. I see Kozluk. I see --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see the word -- big black word "Semberija"?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I got it. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it Ms. Bolton testifying now? Because this way she's forcing the witness too much. He even started mentioning some places, and he said that he isn't comfortable with the map. I -- it seems to me that this is too leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mrs. Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The witness indicated that he crossed over at Bijeljina. He has indicated that he passed through Zvornik. The only difficulty he is having is locating those on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed, and --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the objection is you are now taking over from the witness in trying to locate Bijeljina for him. And I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: But this is not -- this is -- we're dealing with something that is not an issue in dispute. The map of Yugoslavia isn't in dispute in these proceedings, so to assist the witness who is asked for assistance in locating something on a map, this isn't the case where we're asking him to draw something on his own. We're just helping him to read an existing map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Actually, ma'am, if I may just ask, to what extent does the map help if the witness has told us that he crossed through Bijeljina? He's told us that. Do we still have to see Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The only reason I was having him locate -- or trying to have him locate Bijeljina was because when I had asked him about the other map that didn't show Bijeljina, you'd wanted us to indicate where it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Because I thought he would look at the map and see that, "This is where we crossed." Now he doesn't even see the place, and you show him all Janja, Semberija, north, right --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the objection is that actually you are now in the process of locating Bijeljina and not the witness. So -- and the basis of the objection is you're swapping places with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. I'll go back to the other map which we were dealing with because he's now mentioned passing through Zvornik and so forth, and that is visible on the other map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All I'm saying is --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm happy to move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So, sir, if we could then go back to the other map that we were dealing with, which was 2400.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] What do you want to do with this one, Madam Bolton?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Since the a witness wasn't able to identify anything on the map, Your Honour, I don't wish to tender --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] He's just made a marking at a place south-west of Sid.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'd have to look at the transcript for a moment there, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He made a marking, a circle there. If you look at that red border across -- in the middle of the word "Srijem" or whatever that is. Just south-west of Sid, he made that circle there which he first said was Bijeljina. I'm not saying tender it. I just want to know what you want to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I don't wish to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry, sir. I'm now oriented again.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: All right, sir. You had mentioned earlier that you recall passing through Zvornik. Are you able to show us the route you took between Zvornik and Han Pijesak using that -- either the electronic pen on the screen, if you could.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And could we just focus in a little bit closer to area between Zvornik and Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This map on the screen is unreadable, and the map that I have in front of me I can identify it easier.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. I have a print copy -- I want us all to be working on the same map, sir. I have a print copy of the map that's on the screen, and I'd like to provide to you, have you work off of it then. And we can then place it on the ELMO. So you can use your regular pen, sir, instead of the electronic pen on this map.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you please place it on the ELMO, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes. Now -- now we can see it. Can you bring the picture out a little bit further, or is that how ELMO displays it? Can you zoom out any further than that, or is that -- I don't know what the limits of the ELMO are. Okay. Stop, please, and if we can just please -- I'd like Zvornik to be at the top of the screen. That's good there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, can you mark the route you think you took on the 17th July 1995, this being the route you usually took from Zvornik to Han Pijesak? Oh, no, sir. You're going to use the paper copy with your regular pen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And the witness may need assistance holding the paper down. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I took the route. Did you see -- did you see where I went with the pen?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I saw where you went with the pen, sir, but you haven't made any marks with your pen.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And you need to mark all the way to Han Pijesak from Zvornik on the route you took.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. That's not showing up very well. The Registrar has a marker he's going to give you. Sorry. We have all this technology, sir, and give me a paper and pen any day.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And from Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If that could be marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This document becomes Exhibit P2797.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. I'm finished with that document. It's now been marked as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I want to go back and just ask you some questions about the contents of the recording that we were watching at the end of the day yesterday. So I'm going to replay a portion of the recording from July 17th, 1995, in the Han Pijesak boardroom, and then I'll have some questions for you. So we're going to start the recording this time at 25 minutes and 15 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's 9597.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, Your Honour. It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. I'm stopping it at 25 minutes and 45 seconds. What General Mladic has just said there is: "You've come at the moment when our army is engaged in heavy fights around Zepa, and I hope that in the course of the next day the area of Zepa will be solved in the same way as the area of Srebrenica." Can you tell us, do you recall when you first heard of the fighting around Srebrenica or the outcome at Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Certainly. General Mladic was talking about the fact that they were engaged in heavy fights around Zepa and that he hopes that in the course of the next day that Zepa would be solved in the same way as the area of Srebrenica. And I'd like to know when you had first heard mention of the area of Srebrenica having been solved.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall this conversation in detail what he's saying in describing it now. He was discussing that -- that they're fighting in the area and -- and as you said -- you heard what he said. I don't know what you want me to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Was this the first mention you had heard of Srebrenica on that trip in July 1995 of the fact that Srebrenica had been solved?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the first time I heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Who did you hear that from?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard from General Mladic when we were in that boardroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Was anyone else discussing that topic on either -- on July 17th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might have been, but I -- I think it was in -- in the picnic area that -- I think through the discussion, and I cannot specify exactly who said it or -- because to me that wasn't -- to me, it didn't matter any -- mean anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You mentioned you think there was discussion at the picnic area. And what date was that discussion?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that was on the 17th or the 18th. I'm not sure. I cannot remember that precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did you hear General Mladic discuss Srebrenica on more than one occasion?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He might have, but I don't know if I was paying attention to it. Probably did, but as I said, I cannot recall how many time -- I don't think I was counting how many time was mentioning it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Anyone other than General Mladic discussing Srebrenica on -- during this trip?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'd like to refresh your memory from the statement that you provided, the signed statement you provided on September 10th, 2009, at paragraph 12, where you said: "On either the 16th or the 17th of July, I learned that the VRS had liberated Srebrenica. I learned about the victory from General Mladic. His soldiers were also talking about it." Does that now refresh your memory as to whether other people were discussing it as well?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that what I was referring when I said that was the discussion in the -- when we were in the picnic area. That's what I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to continue the tape, sir, a little farther along, and then I'll have some more questions for you. So we're restarting at 25:45.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, I'm stopping the recording at 27 minutes and 19.4 seconds. There General Mladic indicates that he's thanking you for helping us solve our problems with Srebrenica, and to "congratulate you and us on the liberation of the Serbian Srebrenica." What problems did you understand the Bosnian Serb army had been having with Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: What problems?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he was referring to, but I -- I did mention that once in interview -- your interview with me that they had heavy losses around the Srebrenica, Serbian losses, civilians and -- and previously from the Muslims from Srebrenica, and I believe he's referring to that, since Srebrenica is now liberated, that they will not be having intrusion or whatever. This is, like I said, I -- I am assuming. I'm not sure what he meant when he said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: First of all, you indicated that there were intrusions, and they had been having problems with intrusions. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean that the Muslims were heavily located in Srebrenica, and like I said, they -- most of the Serbs around that area, which is Kravica, I heard of a place, and Bratunac and in that area, that -- and they were travelling back and forth from Srebrenica to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did this group of intruders have a name?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know their name. I've never heard their name. Nobody mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Later?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did heard that there was -- their commander was Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And who did you hear about Naser Oric and his -- his group of intruders?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I heard it from General Mladic and -- and I don't know who else. But everybody, I believe, knew that he was in charge of that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: When did you have that discussion with General Mladic about Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have an individual discussion with him, but I think it was his briefing in -- in -- in the room. Either was it outside or inside, I don't know. Was a recorder or not, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: On which date, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Was it 17 or 18, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And he -- you'd indicated that you understood there had been Serbian losses. Were you given any idea of the number of Serbians who had been killed by Naser Oric's group?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got -- I heard it was between 3.000 and 4.000 Serbs in the area was killed by the -- Oric and his -- I don't know what you -- army or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thanks, sir. I'm going to play you another portion of this video that we've been talking about. This is again a portion that I played for you yesterday. It starts at 38 minutes and 41 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you get any sense, sir, from either what a General Mladic said on July 17th or what General Gvero said on July 17th as to the relative importance of the victory at Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What was it? What was your sense?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you heard same as I did. It says that he's appealing to the Serbian unity and importance of this victory that they accomplished.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes. And sorry, my question, sir, was what was your understanding of the relative importance? How important was this victory?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was important because, like I said before, they had heavy losses of civilian population in that area from the Muslim stationed in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: General Gvero said in his speech that the morale of the army at that moment was exceptional. How was the morale at that moment based on your observations of General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see anything usual or different.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: We wouldn't know what his morale is usually so you have to --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: How would I know?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you didn't see any usual or different, then I'll ask the question differently. What was his mood on July 17, 1995?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same as always [indiscernible]. He was always pleasant and nice.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You had told us that he had just had an important victory at Srebrenica. Did he have any -- appear to have any reaction to that?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't show any -- he didn't express to me that I'd see any difference.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to continue the tape, then, sir, at the 48 minute and 43 second mark. This is basically where we left off yesterday at the end of the footage that we've been reviewing today. And this next segment runs from 48 minutes 43 seconds, to 51 minutes and 38 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I'm pausing the tape at 48 minutes and 51 seconds. And there's some objects that General Mladic is handling. Can you tell us what those objects are.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe some car parts. I think oil filter and stuff like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. If we could continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, could you just identify again the name of the gentlemen who's speaking.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, at 50 minutes and 43 seconds.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Branko Zarubin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Were you present during this meeting?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I probably was, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could we backtrack, please, a few seconds, I think to about the 35-second mark or so. Keep going. There we are. Sorry. Okay, so you're -- I'm showing an image at 51.33, and you recognise yourself?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay, and did this take place as indicated in the date, July 18th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And where was this?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Is this a different room than you were in for the footage the previous night or the same room?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the same room. I don't know whether the same room or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have any recollection of the time of day when the car parts and the medication and the money was given to General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: The footage we saw, we were watching previously, this footage July 17th. You told us it was at Crna Rijeka. And you've told us this footage is at Crna Rijeka. Where did you spend the night of the 17th to the 18th?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe we spent in Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: When you spent -- sorry, sir.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I cannot remember where we spent the night.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Were there ever occasions when you spent the night at Crna Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I did spend a couple times in Crna Rijeka, nights.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: When you spent the night at Crna Rijeka, what kind of accommodation would you be in?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was ordinary rooms.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: In what kind of building?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in a -- it's in a kind of in the mountain, building, put in. And I remember one time and I spend the night in a bunker. There was an underground tunnel that they had, and I spend that, but that was, I think, one time in -- it was the wintertime or something.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I have some photographs I'd like to show you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If I could have -- we're going to come back to this tape again, so I'm not seeking to enter it into evidence yet. If we could have 65 ter 9600.21, please. Brief indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are indulged.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, could I have 65 ter 9000.25 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 65 ter?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: 9000.25. Sorry, I thought I said 9600.25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, you didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You had said 9600.21, and then you said 9000.25.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I meant 9600.25. Okay. Could you zoom out again, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Again, sir, I have print copies of those photographs if you would prefer to see a better copy. You see the building in the background, there's some writing on it?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I do see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recognise that building?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Where is that building?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Looking at the right-hand corner of this photo, there's a date stamp 18 July 1995; is that correct, sir? Is that the date?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it down on the bottom, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Is that the date this photo was taken, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And can you assist us in identifying from left to right in the photo the people seated at the picnic table?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Gvero, Ilija Rakanovic, Ned Krayishnik, Ksenija Zarubin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And the object in front of Mrs. Zarubin on the table, can you make that out?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that was her camera.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. What kind of camera?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And the red object on the table?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looks like a telephone.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And how about the white object on the table?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could I have that marked as the next exhibit, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this document becomes Exhibit P2798.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could I please have 65 ter 9600.22. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if we could zoom in to the bottom right-hand corner of this photograph. It's very difficult to read in electronic form. If we could zoom back out, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recall on what date this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Could we have you identify, please, from left to right, the people in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before do you that, can you tell us, that's 18th of what month of what year do you think it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 18th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If you could identify, please, the people from left to right in that photo, just the people that you can -- that are on the far side of the table.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branko Zarubin, General Ratko Mladic, and General Momcilo Perisic, and Ned Krayishnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. That could be tendered as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours this document becomes Exhibit P2799. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If I could please have 9600.21, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: There's a date stamp on the right corner of this photo, sir, 18/7/95. To the best of your recollection, is that date correct?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Starting on the left side of the photo could you identify the three people seated on the left side of the table?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ranko Rakanovic, Ned Krayishnik, and I believe Ksenija Zarubin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And on the right side starting from the gentlemen in the white shirt who is closest to us.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Lesic; general, I believe, I can't see it face -- I would be guessing, General Ratko Mladic and Branko Zarubin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to the gentleman whose face you're having trouble seeing, I'd like to show you a print photograph, as opposed to the computerised image.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If that could be shown to my friend, please. And if it could be shown to the Chamber, please. Now that you have that better image of that photograph, sir, does it assist you in identifying the gentleman in between Mr. Lesic and General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will be guessing, but it looks like General Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If that could be marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted into evidence. May it please be so marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document becomes Exhibit P2800. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I see it is 10.15, Your Honour. Would you like to take the recess?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If it's convenient.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If it's convenient to you, we'll take a break and come back at quarter to. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, the photos we've discussed so far, do you recall approximately what time of day they were taken?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was that question addressed to me?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was fixing my earphones.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: No problem. My question was approximately what time of day, the photos that we've looked at so far, were they taken?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recall whether the photos were taken before or after the footage we watched where the car parts and medication and so forth was given to General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall it exactly. Could it be before, I -- like I said, I really don't know. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall -- first of all, had you ever melt -- you've identified one of the people in the photographs as General Perisic. Had you ever met General Perisic prior to the 18th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Let me continue with some other photos, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If could I have 65 ter 9600.23.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And, sir, if we could zoom in on the bottom right-hand corner, can you read the date stamp on that, or is it too illegible?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall the date of this photo, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was July 18, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And again if you could assist us in identifying from left to right the people seated at the table.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branko Zarubin, General Ratko Mladic, and General Momcilo Perisic, and Ned Krayishnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Were you able to recall at all what -- appear General Mladic was addressing Mr. Zarubin. Do you know what they were talking about?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: General -- you appear to be looking at General Perisic. Were you having any kind of conversation with him?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looks like I was listening that he was talking, but I don't recall what he was -- what were we talked about.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You don't recall what you talked about.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Say that again.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry. You don't recall what you talked about?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recall anything you talked about General Perisic with that day -- about that day?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I made the remark that I was surprised that Muslims made vote to separate from Serbia, and I think he made the remark in that way that he was surprised too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't understand that answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, you want me to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I think I made a remark that I was surprised that the Muslims decided to split from former Yugoslavia, like Bosnia and Herzegovina. And I think General Perisic mentioned that we all kind of was surprised in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And again, can you identify what that white object is on the table?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't -- I can't.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could that be marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This document becomes Exhibit P2801. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If I could next have 65 ter 9600.23. That was it? Sorry, .24. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, again, it's not a great reproduction of the actual photo. Can you read --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Can we zoom in on the bottom right-hand corner of this photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Are you able to read the date stamp from this electronic version of the photo, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Appears to be 18/7/95.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay, if we could zoom back out, please. And again if you could help us identifying the -- first, the person on the left that's cut off in the photo, who was that?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was Branko Zarubin sitting and talking to General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay, and next to General Mladic is?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And the gentleman in the brightly-coloured shirt?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ranko Rakanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If that could be marked the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is so marked. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document becomes Exhibit P2802. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If we could please have 65 ter 9600.25.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, we've already introduced that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could I have .26, please. Sir, again this photograph is a bit blurry. I'm going to ask that you be shown the print version. If I could just show that to my friend, and if it could be shown to the Trial Chamber as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, and on what date was that photo taken, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't seat the date, but I believe it was on the 18th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Is it the same or different day than the other photos that we've been discussing?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry, was it the same or different day than the photos we've already discussed?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it's the same. I don't know. I don't see the date. I can't remember was the same day or -- I believe it was the same day.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Was there more than one occasion that you sat down with General Perisic at the picnic area in Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Might have been. I don't -- by the picture, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. So do you recall another time, then, that you had -- you sat in the picnic area with General Momcilo Perisic at Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to these pictures, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. When was that other occasion, then, that you sat at the picnic area with Momcilo Perisic at Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You'd indicated there may have been another time that you sat at the picnic area with Momcilo Perisic at Han Pijesak, and my question is, what date would that have been?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was the same day.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: So you were at the picnic area with him twice on the same day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be, yeah. Looks -- by the picture, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. What is it about the picture that makes you think there was --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That makes me think that I was sitting on different side of a table.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Was there any time gap? I mean, are we talking about you having been at the tables, going away, coming back to the tables? Or are we talking about you continuously being at the tables but just changing seats?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe we were continuing to be at the table, just changing seats while standing up or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. So just again the building that we see to the left of the photo, what is that building?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's the bidding that goes into -- I don't see the whole building. It looks like -- and it might be the guard, little shadow or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And can you go on the left side of the photo starting with the person who is closest to us and identify the people seated on the left side of the picnic table.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my left is General Milan Gvero, and Ranko Rakanovic and Ned Krayishnik. And the gentleman taking the photograph, Ilija Rakanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay, before you move any further, is there somebody seated in between yourself and Mr. Rakanovic?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between myself and Mr. Rakanovic, no, I don't see anybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What is that dark object to your left?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see any dark object on my left. Let me see down -- on this photo on the table. I don't see any dark object on the table to my left.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Not on the table, just to your left?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, Mrs. Zarubin sitting.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay, there appears to be somebody bent over. Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And the people then on the right side of the table seated?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see General Ratko Mladic and General Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If that could be marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's marked. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document becomes Exhibit P2803. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If we could please have 9600.27.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Again, sir, I think this is similar to a photo we've already seen, but could you identify from left to right the people visible in this photo.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branko Zarubin, General Ratko Mladic, and General Momcilo Perisic, and Ned Krayishnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And again the date of this photo, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime during the day. I don't know what time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, what day are we talking about, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Of?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If we could introduce that as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This becomes Exhibit P2804. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If we could 9600.28, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, can you read the date stamp to the right of this photo?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. 18 --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: July 18th. July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And, sir, there is a person who has his back to the camera. Do you recognise that individual?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looks Ranko Rakanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And the four people going from left to right who are facing the camera?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branko Zarubin, General Ratko Mladic, Milan Lesic, and General Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. All the photos that we've been discussing, you indicated with respect to some of them they were taken at Crna Rijeka. Is that true of all the ones that we've talked about so far?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If I could have 96 -- 65 ter 9469, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want this one admitted, madam?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. Yes, if that could be marked as the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document becomes Exhibit P2805. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks. You now asked for 9469.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, please. And I believe it should be three photos, a series of three photos.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Could -- yes. Sir, do you recognise where this photo was taken?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And the date when this was taken?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: 18th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Bolton, I'm told this photo is under seal. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Oh. Then if we could go into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Oh, P2705.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Admitted from the bar table motion, 2705.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it under seal, Your Honour? Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] That's what the Registrar tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'm just conferring with my colleague. If I may just have a moment's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure you may.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the Registrar was saying while you're conferring, mine the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Oh. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, we should be dealing with these documents in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you say these documents, you mean this photograph and the other two that are part of the series?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. These --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed -- private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you for the indulgence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Returning to the photo that's in front of you then. If you could identify the three people who are -- whose faces are visible to the camera?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my right, Milan Lesic, General Momcilo Perisic, and General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. If we could see the next photograph, please. It should be part of the same exhibit. I'm not sure why we have black and white versions of these photos, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: In any event, if you could again identify, sir, the date and location of -- this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is July 18th, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. And people seated from left to right in this photo?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branko Zarubin, General Ratko Mladic, Milan Lesic, General Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry. And if I could move on to the final photograph in this group.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Again, sir, can you identify the time -- or just the location and the date of -- the date of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the date, but I believe it's 18th of July, 1995. And from left to right, General Ratko Mladic, General Momcilo Perisic, and General Milan Gvero.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And the location again, sir?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm done with those photographs. Thank you. And we could move out of private session then, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, I just want to go back to the first point in the day -- well, first of all, on what date did you first see General Perisic in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: July 18th, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Where was he when you first saw him?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him outside on the picnic area in Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And who was he with when you first saw him?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't call -- recall exactly who was he with when I -- when I got there and when I saw him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you carry on, Mr. Usher, could you please draw the curtain or the blind, as it's called. Thank you so much. Yes, Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I please have ID04-0461. Oh, is it 1D or ID? 1D04-0461. Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, I'd just like to refresh your memory. You indicated you weren't able to tell us who General Perisic was with when you first saw him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: If I could have paragraph 16 of both the English and B/C/S versions this statement from October -- from September 10th, 2009. I should say it was given on September 8th and signed on September 10th. It's actually paragraph 17, page 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Paragraph 17, sir, you indicated at that time, September 10th, shortly before noon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand the Prosecutor may refresh the witness's memory by referring to his statement, but Madam Bolton did not check previously whether the witness remembers the event itself. She just asked one specific question; namely, [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... and who he would been, the first time saw him. [Interpretation] To which the witness answers, he doesn't recall. But she did not continue to ask how he first came into contact with Mr. Perisic. She just refers to the statement of a month ago. I think this is a kind of leading, because the Prosecutor has not ascertained what the witness remembers, if he remembers. In other words, I think it should have been taken step-by-step.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I've asked the witness if he recalled what time of day it was that he met the general, and I also asked him at lines 17 to 18 on page 40 of the transcript, who he was with when you first saw him, and he said he didn't recall. I've asked him some specific questions and now I'm seeking to refresh his memory based on the transcript or the statement he previously gave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It seems as if more than one question was asked, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose that Madam Prosecutor could have also asked questions about chronology and whether the witness remembers a certain event. In any case, I made my objection. I don't want to complicate any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Overruled.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sir, looking at paragraph 17, you indicated in your signed statement that it was: "Shortly before noon, we were called outside for lunch. When we went outside General Mladic was already there with a man he introduced to us as General Momcilo Perisic?" Does that refresh your memory now, sir, as to when and where you first saw General Perisic and who he was with?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was with General Ratko Mladic and General Gvero.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. I don't -- I may use that document again, but I don't want it to be displayed at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What army did you understand General Perisic to be associated with?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yugoslavian army.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And you had indicated you'd visited Han Pijesak before. Had you seen anyone from the Serbian Army there before?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall. I don't remember this before.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see General Perisic arrive at Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To avoid unclarity, page 43, line 2, it says Serbian Army. I suppose the Prosecutor meant the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I was referring, when I asked you the question, about the Serbian Army. Did you understand, sir, I was asking you about the army from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the VJ?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. You indicated you don't know -- or you did not see General Perisic arrive. Did you hear him arrive?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did anybody tell you when he'd arrived?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody told me that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you know how he travelled to Han Pijesak --

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: -- or sorry, Crna Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Did anybody offer any explanation as to what General Perisic was doing there?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody did explain anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: When you were seated at the picnic tables, what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sitting at a picnic table.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: What was the group of people doing?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Group of people are those that I identified in the picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: No, what were people doing as they were seated at the table? I know who was seated at the table.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were sitting and talking.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. How long were you in, first of all, that day General Mladic's company in total, all of July 18th?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall exact timing. Probably couple hours. I'm guessing.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: And how about General Perisic's company?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same time. I'm guessing again. I could not recall the timing because I was not keep any diary of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. At any point in time we saw that you were seated with General Perisic at the picnic tables, did General Perisic ever absent himself from the tables in your presence? Sorry, that was a confusing question. While you were at the picnics tables, did General Perisic ever get up and leave?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: How did Generals Perisic and Mladic appear to be getting along?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normal, like every -- everybody else in that area. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Were there any signs of disagreement between them?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: You said people were talking. What was the general mood at the tables?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: A normal mood.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Okay. What are you -- what do you consider a normal mood?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same as we are in this room.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Same kind of tone?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just talking wasn't in a -- talking whoever you were close to or listening to somebody else and ...

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Was there any laughter?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There might have been. I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recall what was discussed?

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Do you recall any conversation between General Gvero and General Mladic -- Mladic, sorry.

utterances.speaker: NED KRAYISHNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.
